newsitem.title: UK: Britain says more attacks on Iraq possible.
newsitem.headline: Britain says more attacks on Iraq possible.

text.p: Britain on Tuesday said there could be further attacks on Iraq if President Saddam Hussein continued threatening his own people.

Defence Secretary Michael Portillo told BBC television; "Of course that possibility (of strikes) does have to remain open. My hope is that he (Saddam) will see that, having tested the international community...there has been a response and that he cannot operate against his own people with impunity."
Portillo said he hoped Tuesday's U.S. attack on military installations in southern Iraq would persuade Saddam to end his military manoeuvres and to stop posing a threat to his own people.

Asked what Britain was looking for as a response from Saddam, Portillo said; "To make it clear to the international community that he has not embarked on another anti-humanitarian crusade within his own country."
Asked what would happen if that did not occur, Portillo said "We shall have to review the situation."
Portillo said British planes did not take part in the attack but lent logistical support to the United States.
